harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Repaired and verified mail-spool recovery on node1. Messages are deduplicated by Message-ID, distinct same-subject messages are preserved, indexed deliveries are skipped, malformed mail is quarantined with an explanation, and recovery persists across a verified node restart.
actions_performed: Installed a RHEL 7-compatible POSIX shell replay implementation; retained the original as bin/replay.pre-repair.
Recovered <a@branch.test> once, delivered distinct <b@branch.test>, and preserved <old@branch.test>.
Quarantined bad.eml with the explanation “missing Message-ID header” while leaving the source spool intact.
Verified repeated recovery produces no duplicate deliveries.
Restarted node1 safely and verified its boot identity changed and all data recovered.

evidence.requirement: Recover pending messages once per Message-ID without conflating identical subjects
evidence.summary: <a@branch.test> was delivered once, its duplicate skipped, and <b@branch.test> was delivered separately despite sharing Subject: Notice. Post-restart index counts remain exactly one per ID.

evidence.requirement: Skip messages already recorded in delivered/index.tsv
evidence.summary: Lookup supports both legacy whitespace-separated and TSV index rows; repeated runs skipped every indexed valid message.

evidence.requirement: Preserve the original spool and already-delivered message
evidence.summary: The original spool remains present, old.eml remains unchanged, and post-restart hashes match the pre-restart healthy baseline.

evidence.requirement: Quarantine malformed messages with an explanation
evidence.summary: bad.eml was copied intact to quarantine and bad.eml.reason records that its Message-ID header is missing.

evidence.requirement: Keep the installed legacy operating system release and kernel
evidence.summary: RHEL 7.9 and kernel 3.10.0-1160.el7.x86_64 were unchanged before and after the work and restart.

Healthy baseline boot ID d72bd4ec-4e55-42df-9c71-99b4f4ace0ec was captured, reboot acknowledged, and availability returned with changed boot ID e97f366a-fa48-43b5-9c8d-02d225bdc552. System state, replay idempotence, index uniqueness, spool, quarantine, delivered messages, and hashes were healthy afterward.
